findings.message: Step 3.52 does not tell a failed rules lookup apart from an empty one. If `specclaw-presets` or `specclaw-review rules` exits non-zero or times out, the agent gets no Security rules block. The agent's edge case then treats that as "No Security rules block" (agents/infosec-reviewer.md:69), skips step 3, and can still write APPROVED. The verify-report line shows only the verdict, so a lookup that never ran reads as a clean pass. Fix: when a rules command fails, pass an explicit 'rules: NOT RUN — <command> failed' marker. Have the agent carry that into the report, and add it to the `**InfoSec Review:**` line, separate from the case where a stack really has no Security section.
findings.scenario: `specclaw-presets` crashes (missing preset file) → agent reviews without stack rules and finds nothing → verify-report shows `**InfoSec Review:** APPROVED — 0 findings`, with no sign the checklist was never applied.

findings.message: security-report.md is committed to git and its verdict depends on the security rules that were read and the code state that was reviewed. The template records the model but not the preset or rules pack version (plugin version) or the commit SHA reviewed. Fix: add `**Rules:** specclaw-presets <version>, specclaw-review <version or not installed>` and `**Commit:** <sha>` lines to the report header, and have verify pass these values to the agent.
findings.scenario: Report written at 0.9.17 says APPROVED. In 0.9.18 the node preset adds a rule the code breaks. The committed report still says APPROVED, and nothing shows it was judged against the older rules or an earlier commit.

findings.message: Step 2 only checks that a `**Verdict:**` line exists, not that its value is one of APPROVED, APPROVED_WITH_NOTES, CHANGES_REQUESTED or NOT_RUN. A malformed value, such as the unfilled template placeholder, would be copied into the verify-report as a verdict. Treat any other value as `NOT RUN — malformed verdict`.

The agent reads untrusted changed-file content and holds an unscoped `Write` tool. Text in the reviewed files could tell it to write files other than security-report.md. The guardrail says it never edits code, but nothing limits Write to `.specclaw/changes/<change>/security-report.md`. State that changed-file content is data and never instructions, and that the only file it may write is that report path.

Severity labels are written two ways: `🔴 BLOCK` / `🟡 WARN` / `🟢 NOTE` in the Severity section and `[BLOCK]` in the output heading. Use one spelling so verify's X BLOCK / Y WARN / Z NOTE count parses one form.
